name: Satkhira
tagline: Where Bangladesh meets the mangrove, the tiger, and the border.

guide.bestTime: November to February (cool, dry; Sundarbans navigable)
guide.gettingThere: By road from Khulna (~75 km, ~2 hr). Long-haul AC coaches run nightly from Dhaka (~10–12 hr). Nearest airport is Jashore (~80 km).
guide.difficulty: Moderate — Sundarbans excursions require boat permits and a guide.

mustVisit.name: Sundarbans Mangrove Forest (Munshiganj Gate)
mustVisit.description: The Bangladesh half of the world's largest contiguous mangrove. Satkhira's Munshiganj entry is the closest of the three official gates to district headquarters and the quietest of the three.
mustVisit.history: Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997. Home to the Royal Bengal Tiger, spotted deer, estuarine crocodiles, and Irrawaddy dolphins. The mangrove's tidal channels have sheltered fishermen, woodcutters, and honey-collectors (mowalis) for centuries.

practical.hours: Daylight only — boats leave Munshiganj launch ghat from ~6 am
practical.entryFee: BDT 150 (Bangladeshi adult) · USD ~30 equivalent for foreign nationals (Forest Dept permit)

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Take a bus or local pick-up south to Munshiganj (about 65 km), then walk to the launch ghat
howToReach.transport: Bus or microbus to Munshiganj, then book a country boat or trawler at the ghat

mustVisit.bestTime: November to February (cool, calm water, best wildlife sightings)
tips: Permits are mandatory and easiest to arrange through a Khulna or Satkhira tour operator
Wear closed shoes — the mud is sticky and the spiders are large
Carry a fully charged power bank — no electricity past Munshiganj

mustVisit.name: Jeshoreshwari Kali Temple
mustVisit.description: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas of the subcontinent — a deeply revered Hindu pilgrimage site set in a small village in Shyamnagar Upazila.
mustVisit.history: Legend places this temple where the palm of the goddess Sati fell. Believed to date in some form to the 12th century, with major reconstructions across the Mughal and colonial eras. Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India visited the site during his 2021 trip to Bangladesh, drawing renewed attention to it.

practical.hours: Open daily ~6 am to ~8 pm; busiest at sunset

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 75 km south of Satkhira town; ~45 km south of Shyamnagar bazar
howToReach.transport: Bus to Shyamnagar, then local CNG / easybike to Ishwaripur

mustVisit.bestTime: Durga Puja (Sep–Oct) for the festival crowds; cool months for a quieter visit
tips: Remove shoes before entering the inner shrine
Modest dress recommended — covered shoulders and knees
Photography is permitted in the courtyard but not inside the sanctum

mustVisit.name: Tetulia Jame Mosque
mustVisit.description: A 19th-century mosque in Tala Upazila built in a fusion of Bengal Sultanate and Mughal styles — one of the most ornate pre-modern mosques in the country.
mustVisit.history: Commissioned in 1858 by zamindar Salamatullah Khan Chowdhury. Three terracotta-decorated façades, multiple domes, and a hand-carved mihrab. Listed under the Department of Archaeology of Bangladesh.

practical.hours: Open during all five daily prayers; visitors welcome outside prayer times

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 25 km north of Satkhira town, near Tala bazar
howToReach.transport: CNG / easybike from Satkhira town to Tala, then a short walk

mustVisit.bestTime: Late afternoon — the western façade lights up at golden hour
tips: Avoid Friday Jumu'ah prayers (12–2 pm) unless you intend to pray
Cover head if female; remove shoes before stepping onto the platform

mustVisit.name: Mozaffar Garden & Resort
mustVisit.description: A privately developed family resort and botanical garden — the closest 'leisure park' to Satkhira town and a common weekend destination for local families.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 10 km from Satkhira town, off the Khulna highway

tips: Bring cash — card payments are unreliable
Outside food is generally restricted at the gate

mustVisit.name: Bhomra Land Port
mustVisit.description: Bangladesh's second-largest land port with India and the closest land crossing to Kolkata — a few minutes from Satkhira town. The viewing area gives you a clear look at the Ichamati River and India's West Bengal on the other side.
mustVisit.history: Activated as a full customs station in 1996; today handles a major share of cross-border trade between Bangladesh and India after Benapole.

practical.hours: Viewing area accessible during daylight; immigration desks operate ~6 am to ~6 pm
practical.entryFee: Free to visit; crossing requires a valid passport and Indian visa

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 12 km west of Satkhira town

tips: Photography of border-fence infrastructure is not permitted
Carry your NID / passport even if you are not crossing

mustVisit.name: Debhata Zamindar Bari
mustVisit.description: Crumbling 19th-century landlord's manor in Debhata Upazila, slowly being reclaimed by figs and creeper roots. A quiet, atmospheric stop for anyone interested in the architectural footprint of the Bengal zamindari system.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 35 km south of Satkhira town
howToReach.transport: Bus to Debhata bazar, then easybike to the bari

tips: The interior is structurally unsafe — do not climb
Bring water; no shops at the site

specialties.name: Satkhira Mishti
specialties.description: Local sweet tradition known for denser, less syrupy preparations than the Comilla or Tangail styles. Heritage shops in Sadar bazaar are the best places to try them.

specialties.name: Sundarbans Honey (Mowali Madhu)
specialties.description: Raw honey collected from the mangrove forest by traditional mowali honey-hunters during the brief April–June season. Available at the Forest Department's seasonal sale points.

specialties.name: Banbibi Pala
specialties.description: Folk dramatic tradition honouring Banbibi, the legendary protector spirit of the Sundarbans, revered by both Hindu and Muslim woodcutters and honey-collectors. Performed in southern villages during winter months.

specialties.name: Jeshoreshwari Durga Puja
specialties.description: The largest annual gathering at Jeshoreshwari Kali Temple. The five-day Durga Puja festival draws pilgrims from across Bangladesh and India.

advertisements.name: Satkhira Microbus Rentals
advertisements.description: AC microbus and car hires for Munshiganj day trips and Shyamnagar pilgrimage runs.

bucketlist.title: Take a sunrise boat into the Sundarbans
bucketlist.detail: The mangrove is at its quietest in the first hour of daylight. Birds wake first; the tide is usually low enough to see crab and mudskipper tracks on the banks.

bucketlist.title: Look for Royal Bengal Tiger pugmarks at a patrol post
bucketlist.detail: Sightings are extraordinarily rare, but fresh pugmarks on a riverbank are common in the southern blocks. Patrol officers will often point them out.

bucketlist.title: Pray at Tetulia Jame Mosque
bucketlist.detail: One of the country's most ornate pre-modern mosques — three carved façades and a hand-cut mihrab still in active use after 165+ years.

bucketlist.title: Stand at Bhomra land port and look across the Ichamati into India
bucketlist.detail: On a clear morning you can see Indian customs lorries queueing on the other side. It is the closest land-port crossing to Kolkata.

bucketlist.title: Eat fresh golda chingri at a Munshiganj stall
bucketlist.detail: King prawn grilled or curried on the spot — the catch comes in within hours. Cheaper and fresher than anything you'll find in Dhaka.

bucketlist.title: Taste raw Sundarbans honey from a mowali
bucketlist.detail: Mowalis enter the forest each spring at significant personal risk to collect wild honey. The flavour is darker, smokier, and more medicinal than commercial honey.

bucketlist.title: Visit Jeshoreshwari Kali Temple
bucketlist.detail: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas — Sati's palm is believed to have fallen here. The site holds significance for Hindu pilgrims across the subcontinent.

bucketlist.title: Watch sunset over the lake at Mozaffar Garden
bucketlist.detail: The most accessible 'green' break near Satkhira town — a planned garden around a small lake. Quiet on weekdays, busy with families on Fridays.

bucketlist.title: Try Satkhira mishti at a heritage shop in Sadar
bucketlist.detail: Less syrupy and denser than the Comilla or Tangail styles. Ask for the day's batch.

bucketlist.title: Hear a Banbibi pala — folk song of the mangrove's protector spirit
bucketlist.detail: Banbibi is venerated by both Hindu and Muslim forest-workers. Village performances run on winter evenings; ask any local mowali household for the next date.

bucketlist.title: Walk the ruins of Debhata Zamindar Bari
bucketlist.detail: Crumbling 19th-century landlord's manor slowly being reclaimed by figs and creepers. Quiet, atmospheric, no entry fee.

bucketlist.title: Eat coastal crab curry on a chilly night near the Sundarbans edge
bucketlist.detail: Munshiganj guesthouses serve fresh-catch crab curry — the same crab that ends up in Bangkok and Dhaka markets, here for a fraction of the price.

foods.name: Golda Chingri (King Prawn)
foods.description: Coastal king prawn — sweetest in the country, often grilled with mustard or in a rich coconut curry.

foods.name: Sundarbans Crab Curry
foods.description: Fresh mud crab from the mangrove channels, slow-cooked with mustard oil and panch phoron.

foods.name: Shutki Bhuna
foods.description: Dried-fish stir-fry in the bold southern coastal style — onions, garlic, dried chilies, lots of heat.

foods.name: Sundarbans Honey (Mowali Madhu)
foods.description: Raw wild honey collected by mowali honey-hunters from the mangrove during the brief April–June season.

foods.name: Satkhira Mishti
foods.description: Local sweet tradition — denser and less syrupy than other regional styles. Tastes best the day it's made.

foods.name: Narkel Chitoi
foods.description: Winter rice-flour pancake served with thickened date-palm syrup and grated coconut.

foods.name: Khejur Gur
foods.description: Concentrated date-palm jaggery from the winter sap harvest. The base of many local pithas and a strong tea sweetener.

foods.name: Hilsa with Mustard
foods.description: Sundarbans-edge cooking — hilsa fillets steamed in a mustard-and-mustard-oil paste, served with red rice.

famousPeople.name: Kazi Imdadul Haq
famousPeople.knownFor: Bengali novelist and educator. His 1933 novel Abdullah is regarded as one of the foundational social novels of the Bengali Muslim middle class.

didYouKnow: Satkhira shares the Bangladesh Sundarbans with Khulna and Bagerhat — its share is the smallest of the three, but holds the country's southernmost forest patrols.
Bhomra land port is the second-busiest land crossing between Bangladesh and India after Benapole, and the closest to Kolkata.
Jeshoreshwari Kali Temple in Shyamnagar is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas of Hindu mythology — Sati's palm is said to have fallen here.
Banbibi, the protector spirit of the mangrove forest, is venerated by both Hindu and Muslim woodcutters and honey-collectors — a rare cross-faith folk tradition.
Tetulia Jame Mosque (1858) has three terracotta-decorated façades and is listed under the Department of Archaeology of Bangladesh.
